podcast.title: Dominance in Late 70s Music
podcast.body: Founded by Neil Bogart, Casablanca Records emerged as a dominant force in the music business during the late 1970s. Bogart's vision, including his request for the extended version of "Love to Love You Baby," played a crucial role in shaping disco's commercial success and popularizing new recording formats. "the label that would come to dominate the music business in the late 70s."

podcast.title: Neil Bogart's "I Feel Love" Insight
podcast.body: Neil Bogart of Casablanca Records was instrumental in the release of Donna Summer's "I Feel Love" as a single, despite neither Summer nor producer Giorgio Moroder initially believing it should be released that way. "It was never going to be released as a single until Neil Bogart of Casa Blanca Records said that it should be."

podcast.title: Role in "Love to Love You Baby" Development
podcast.body: Casablanca Records, founded by Neil Bogart, played a crucial role in the creation of the extended 17-minute version of Donna Summer's "Love to Love You Baby." Bogart's vision for a long-form song conducive to lovemaking led him to request the extended version from Giorgio Moroder, shaping the song's iconic status. "Neil Bogart, the founder of Casa Blanca Records, was given that record by George Eoma Rotor, one of Donna Summer's producers and a Disco genius, by the way."
